task.description:
Write test spec at tests/specs/DSL-05.md covering the coercion test matrix as a comprehensive set of unit tests for src/expr/mod.zig evaluateNode(). The spec must cover:

1. Arithmetic coercion (add_expr, mul_expr, unary_neg):
   - int64 + int64 → int64
   - float64 + float64 → float64
   - int64 + float64 → float64 (promotion)
   - float64 + int64 → float64 (promotion)
   - Non-numeric + numeric → EvalError
   - null in arithmetic → EvalError

2. Comparison with no silent coercion:
   - int64 == int64 → bool
   - float64 < float64 → bool
   - int64 == float64 → EvalError (different types)
   - string == string → bool
   - bool != bool → bool
   - Different types compared → EvalError

3. Three-valued null comparison:
   - null == null → true
   - null != null → false
   - null == 42 → null
   - null != 42 → null
   - null < 42 → null
   - null <= 42 → null
   - null > 42 → null
   - null >= 42 → null
   - null == true → null
   - null == "hello" → null

4. Three-valued boolean logic:
   - null AND true → null
   - null AND false → false
   - null OR true → true
   - null OR false → null
   - true AND null → null
   - false OR null → null
   - NOT null → null
   - null AND null → null
   - null OR null → null

5. No automatic string coercion:
   - "42" + 1 → EvalError
   - "42" == 42 → EvalError
   - 1 + "1" → EvalError

Write the test source code into src/expr/mod.zig as additional test blocks (DSL-05 section).
acceptance_criteria: All type pairs × operator categories have a dedicated test
Three-valued null logic tested for all operators
No silent coercion in comparisons verified by tests expecting EvalError
All tests are unit tests (no I/O, no DB, no external dependencies)

result.summary: Wrote test spec at tests/specs/DSL-05.md (78 test cases across arithmetic, comparison, boolean logic, unary operators, dot-path, and no-string-coercion categories). Reviewed existing 46 DSL-05 tests in src/expr/mod.zig; added 19 missing tests covering: negate string/timestamp, null >=/<=/== with non-null types, ordering null>null/null>=null, int64!=float64/float64==int64/string==int64/bool==string cross-type comparison errors, false-and-null/true-or-null short-circuit, 5-and-true/5-or-false non-boolean left operand, 1+"1"/"a"+"b"/"42"==42 no-auto-coercion, and float64/0.0 IEEE 754 infinity.
